thread:
Maria: threw together a small proposal to make 'state ownership' explicit in ServingManifests. goal: eliminate adapter heuristics and make migrations safe. paste below and asking for ops + privacy feedback.

Raj: quick summary? what breaks for customers?

Maria: in short: add `state_ownership` enum to spec (controlplane | runtime | hybrid). defaults per mode, explicit migration block for ownership changes. makes behavior declarative instead of implicit.

Ana: can we see an example manifest snippet for private? private is the trickiest.

Maria: sure — snippet: 
``napiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: ServingManifest
metadata:
  tenant: acme
spec:
  mode: private
  model: gpt-small-v2
  state_ownership: controlplane  # controlplane | runtime | hybrid
  ksms: ["projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/serving"]
  fallback_policy:
    - prefer: runtime
      when: cpu_util > 0.85
```
(please note: backticks where appropriate in RFC)

Liam: important: for private, default to `runtime` to respect air-gapped customers unless they opt into a `controlplane_link`. otherwise we force KMS exposure.

Ana: +1. If someone sets controlplane in private, require `controlplane_link: true` and documented KMS proxy configuration.

SRE Oncall: perf note: switching ownership affects cross-node calls and token latency. runtime-owned leases reduce controlplane RPCs but increase runtime CPU/IO. we should run perf sims before enabling wide rollout.

Raj: how do we prevent split-brain during rollout if ownership flips mid-deploy? current fallback adapters assume single source of truth.

Maria: add `ownership_migration` block required for any manifest that changes ownership. it must include `drain_timeout` and `consistency_mode`. sample: 
``nownership_migration:
  from: controlplane
  to: runtime
  drain_timeout: 120s
  consistency_mode: graceful
```
Validators reject migrations missing required fields or unsafe defaults.

Ana: validators should enforce `drain_timeout >= 60s` and `consistency_mode` in [graceful, strict] for safety.

Liam: telemetry question: who emits tenant metrics when controlplane owns state? plan: controlplane emits for hosted/dedicated; for private runtime emits. add `metrics_forwarding: true|false` flag, default false for private.

SRE Oncall: agree default false to avoid unintentional data leakage. add runbook entries for alerts like `double-lease-detected` and `migration-failure`.

Raj: adapter work: small shim to read `state_ownership` and toggle lease codepath. estimate ~3 engineer-weeks across runtime + controlplane adapters.

Dev Bot: unit tests for manifest parser ✅ all green (local).

Ana: dependency for controlplane in private: KMS proxy + docs for provisioning. I'll draft the doc.

Maria: proposed rollout plan: 1) RFC with migration guidelines + validator rules (I'll draft) 2) shim prototype + unit tests (Raj/Ana) 3) perf sims & SLO impact analysis (Liam + SRE) 4) Console UX: surface `state_ownership` and migration status 5) Support playbook & runbook.

Liam: add a short rollback checklist for support: how to revert an ownership migration, steps to force drain, and alert thresholds to watch.

SRE Oncall: add synthetic checks to detect lease divergence and a throttled automated revert for obvious splits.

Raj: I'll scope the shim PR and post a timeline by EOD.

Ana: I'll start KMS proxy docs and a private-mode caveats section.

Maria: thanks all — will open RFC in docs/rfcs and tag here. :white_check_mark:
